{"actions": [{"kd": 0, "ki": 0, "kind": "swap_machine_part", "kp": 0, "target": "pelvis__act", "value": "ds3218", "why": "Strongest listed option at 21.5 kg·cm, versus 11.01 kg·cm for the MG996R."}], "mode": "suggested", "reply": "Do not build this version yet. No listed part fully fixes it.

The closest listed improvement is the DS3218: 21.5 kg·cm at 6.8 V, versus the MG996R stall torque of 11.01 kg·cm. I have suggested that swap only as a partial step. It still fails the pelvis at 22.0 kg·cm, and is far below the torso shell at 26.6 kg·cm, shoulder yoke at 31.6 kg·cm, left upper arm at 44.3 kg·cm, left thigh at 112.7 kg·cm, and torso core at 173.9 kg·cm.

What you actually need is:
- Actuators outside the listed options, rated well above 173.9 kg·cm for the largest load, or a much lighter structure and shorter lever arms.
- A stronger left hip yaw actuator: it needs 114.8 kg·cm, while the CubeMars AK60-6 stalls at 91.74 kg·cm. Every listed hobby-servo replacement is 21.5 kg·cm or less.
- A power supply rated above the 17.9 A peak at the required actuator voltages. The present supply is delivering about 0 A, and no listed option covers 17.9 A.
- Relief for the waist joints, currently at 96 % and 75 % of stall torque. Above about 60 % they will run hot and wear quickly.

In short: get stronger actuators, lighten or shorten the structure, and upgrade the supply first. The suggested DS3218 swap alone will not make this robot pass."}
